A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same ECTS survey and benchmark. Their complete main texts, figures, tables, equations, and appendices support reliable comparison despite substantial reorganization.

before.justification: v3 Section 4 and Appendix C report original benchmark experiments, calibration and classifier studies, and analyses of normalization and decision costs.

after.justification: v6 retains original benchmark results and adds end-to-end comparisons, an anticipation ablation, and quantitative dataset and classifier analyses.

M1.justification: The primary algorithms, baseline definitions, and TeaserAvg adaptation are retained. Revised method descriptions and the diagnostic myopic variants do not establish a changed primary method.

E1.justification: The reported non-normalized collection decreases from 35 to 34 datasets, with InsectEPGRegularTrain omitted from v6 Table 7. The 77-dataset UCR benchmark and task families remain. However, Appendix F.6 still reports normalization results on 35 datasets, so the removal is not consistently reflected throughout v6.

E2.justification: v3 explicitly excludes end-to-end methods from its experiments. v6 Appendix C.2 evaluates EARLIEST and ELECTS against Proba Threshold, extending comparisons to an additional architectural family. The main separable comparator set remains unchanged.

E3.justification: The stated classifier/trigger training allocation changes from 60%/40% to 40%/60%, and Stopping Rule's grid size changes from 990 to 1000. The new end-to-end comparison permits finer prediction times than the separable baseline's 20 timestamps. These are reported protocol differences; the PDFs do not establish which retained experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: v6 Appendix F.4 directly tests anticipation by restricting Economy's horizon and Calimera's backward cost propagation to one step. Table 7 adds dataset-level AUC-gain evidence, and Table 8 quantifies classifier first-place frequencies. The earlier calibration, normalization, classifier-substitution, and cost-decomposition analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions report 90% bootstrap confidence intervals using 10,000 resamples, Wilcoxon-Holm comparisons, and pairwise Wilcoxon tests. No changed training-run counts, seed reporting, or uncertainty-estimation procedure is documented.

E6.justification: v6 adds end-to-end rankings, myopic-ablation results, dataset AUC gains, and classifier comparison percentages. Anomaly-setting AvgCost values at alpha=0.5 change, including Economy from 6.03 to 6.21 and Calimera from 6.02 to 6.20. Changed corpus and protocol descriptions prevent interpreting these as identical-setting performance differences. The main standard-setting results are retained.

T1.justification: v3 Section 3.3's formal reinforcement-learning development, including the Q-function, optimal-policy, and action-selection equations, is removed. v6 Appendix C retains descriptions of those methods without that development. The central cost and optimal-stopping framework remains.

C1.justification: v6 explicitly narrows the abstract and contribution framing to separable ECTS methods, whereas v3 presents a broader ECTS taxonomy. The principal contributions remain a taxonomy, a shared benchmark methodology, and an open-source library; v3's main experiments already focused on separable methods.

C2.justification: v6 explains the end-to-end methods' high-delay-cost advantage through their finer prediction-time resolution, limiting architectural conclusions. It also interprets the new ablation as showing why anticipation matters more when waiting is inexpensive, and expands discussion of stochastic costs and cost drift.

D1.justification: New Appendix D documents the library's component interfaces and provides usage code. Appendix B.4 specifies the previously qualitative dataset-selection requirement through early-versus-late training AUC, and Appendix F.4 supplies the ablation implementation details. The experiment-code repository changes, while Table 7 replaces individual train/test counts with total sizes.

R1.justification: v6 adds explicit positioning against earlier surveys and a systematic table comparing published benchmarking protocols. It introduces discussion of FIRMBOUND, CIS, and non-independent sequential-testing extensions, and expands Benefitter beyond its earlier table entry. This substantially develops the rationale and research context for the benchmark.

P1.justification: The title, introduction, conclusion, and taxonomy narrative are extensively revised. Protocol details move into Appendix B, end-to-end and shapelet discussions are reorganized into Appendix C, and related-benchmark and library appendices are added. These are substantial structural and editorial changes beyond added experiments.

P2.justification: v6 redraws the taxonomy and experiment diagrams, separates the method tables, adds two experimental figures and new comparison tables, and expands the dataset table with AUC columns. The publication layout substantially reflows text and existing figures, although most original benchmark graphics are reused.

improvement.justification: The direct anticipation ablation, quantitative dataset audit, and clearer research positioning make important claims easier to assess, while the library documentation improves usability. These gains are limited by unresolved reporting inconsistencies: v6's 34-dataset collection conflicts with its retained 35-dataset normalization analysis, and Section 4.3.1 gives a delay-cost endpoint of 100 times alpha that contradicts Figure 5's formula.
